# Reid Design LLC — Full Site Content

> Reid Design LLC is a residential interior design studio in Plainfield, Indiana, run by Staci Perkins. It serves homeowners in Plainfield, Indianapolis, and the surrounding suburbs (Carmel, Fishers, Westfield, Zionsville, Noblesville) with warm, livable, mid-market design. Services run from a $150 in-home consultation up to full room design, styling, shopping and sourcing, and online E-Design. Pricing is shown openly on the site.

This is the expanded companion to /llms.txt. It inlines the substantive content of the site so a language model can answer questions about Reid Design from a single document. For the short link map, see /llms.txt.

## Services and pricing

### In-home consultation — $150
A 60 to 90 minute in-home visit where we walk your space, talk through what's not working, and leave you with a clear plan.
Best for: Homeowners who know something feels off but aren't sure where to start.

- 60 to 90 minute in-home visit
- Layout assessment and guidance
- Color and finish direction (includes paint color help and sample testing)
- Clear next-steps plan

### E-Design — starting at $450
A fully digital design package for clients outside Greater Indianapolis or who prefer to manage the install themselves.
Best for: Out-of-area clients, hands-on homeowners, or anyone who wants a clear plan without the in-home install.

- Full digital design plan delivered as a clickable PDF
- Mood board + finish/material palette
- 2D layout with furniture placement
- Sourcing list with direct shopping links
- One round of revisions
- Two weeks of email follow-up while you shop

### Full room design — starting at $650
A complete plan for one room — layout, furniture, decor, paint direction, and a sourcing list with direct shopping links. You shop at your own pace.
Best for: A single-room reset where you want a plan you can act on at your own pace.

- Layout and furniture placement
- Mood board and concept direction
- Furniture and decor recommendations
- Color palette and finish guidance
- Curated sourcing list with shopping links
- One revision round

### Full room design + styling — starting at $850
Everything in Full Room Design, plus me on the ground — shopping with you, picking paint, hanging the art, styling the shelves.
Best for: When you'd rather hand the project off than manage it.

- Everything in Full Room Design
- Hands-on shopping and sourcing
- Paint color selections
- Rug, art, and styling direction
- In-home styling and final reveal

### Shopping & sourcing — $75 per hour
Help finding the right pieces — billed hourly, no minimum, trade-vendor access included.
Best for: When you have the vision and just need the right finds.

- Trade-only and retail vendor sourcing
- Curated finds matched to your style
- Shopping coordination and in-store visits
- Vendor and lead-time management

### Builder & realtor partnerships — Custom
For builders, realtors, and contractors in the Plainfield and Indianapolis area. Finish selections, staging, move-in styling — whatever the project needs.
Best for: Builders, realtors, and contractors looking for a design partner.

- Finish selections and fixture packages for new construction
- Staging for listings and move-in styling for buyers
- Design-side coordination for renovation projects

## How a project works

### Step 1: In-home consultation (Single visit)
A free intro chat to make sure we're a fit, then a 60 to 90 minute in-home visit to walk your space and build a clear plan.

### Step 2: Design plan created (2 to 3 weeks)
Mood board, layout, furniture and decor selections, and a sourcing list with direct shopping links. You see everything before anything is purchased.

### Step 3: Shopping + selections (Per project scope)
You shop the curated list at your own pace, or I source and order it for you. Trade vendor access is included either way.

### Step 4: Styling + final reveal (Final visit)
Everything gets placed, styled, and accessorized. Then I step back, you walk in. This is the moment.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need to buy all new furniture?
Not at all. I love working with pieces you already own, a room that incorporates meaningful things feels more personal than one that's entirely new. We'll identify what's worth keeping, what can be repurposed, and what genuinely needs to go.

### What's your background as a designer?
Staci is still updating this one. The short version: she's a Plainfield-based interior designer running Reid Design as a one-person studio. If background matters for your project, ask in the contact form and she'll get into it personally.

### Are you available for commercial projects?
My primary focus is residential, but I'm open to small commercial spaces, boutiques, offices, short-term rentals. Reach out and describe your project.

### Do you work with contractors?
For full-service projects involving renovation, I coordinate with contractors but don't act as a general contractor. I can provide referrals to trusted tradespeople in the Indianapolis area and manage design-side communication.

### What if something arrives damaged?
For full-service clients where I manage purchasing, I handle all claims, returns, and reorders. Vendor relationships and trade accounts come with better resolution processes than retail. I deal with it so you don't have to.

### What if I don't like the design plan?
Every package includes one full revision round. The thorough consultation up front means major revisions are rare, but the protection is always there. Nothing gets ordered until you give explicit approval.

### What happens on the first conversation?
The intro conversation is short, free, and completely informal. We trade a few notes about your space, goals, rough budget, and timeline, by phone or message, whichever is easier for you. My main goal is to figure out whether I'm the right fit for your project. There's no pitch and no pressure. If we're a fit, we book the in-home consultation from there.

### Who's a good fit, and who's not?
Reid Design is a great fit if you want a designer who listens, works with what you already have when it makes sense, and is honest about what things cost. It's probably not the right fit if you want a fully hands-off luxury experience, or if you're looking for someone to act as a general contractor on a major renovation. If you're unsure, the intro call is the easiest way to figure out together whether we should work together.

### Are there hidden fees I should know about?
No. The design fee is stated upfront before any work begins. The only additional cost is the furnishings and materials you choose to purchase, and you're always in control of that budget. For full-service clients, trade vendor markups are disclosed transparently at the start. For homes outside the local area, a small travel fee may apply, always quoted upfront before booking.

### How much does interior design cost in Indianapolis?
Costs vary by scope. At Reid Design: an in-home consultation is $150 for a 60 to 90 minute session. Full Room Design starts at $650 and includes a complete design plan with mood direction, layout, furniture and decor selections, and a sourcing list with direct shopping links. Full Room Design + Styling starts at $850 and adds hands-on shopping, paint color selections, and an in-home styling and final reveal. Hourly Shopping & Sourcing is $75 per hour, no minimum. Full-service and custom whole-home projects are quoted after the consultation. The Indianapolis market generally runs $50 to $200 per hour for hourly work, with full room packages from $1,000 to $5,000.

### How involved do I need to be during the project?
As involved as you want. Some clients love seeing every decision. Others hand it off completely and want to be surprised at the reveal. Both are valid. The one non-negotiable: you review and approve the design plan before anything is purchased.

### Do I need to know my style before reaching out?
Absolutely not. Most clients can't articulate their style cleanly, that's part of what the consultation uncovers. If you have a Pinterest board or Instagram saves, bring those. If you have nothing, that's fine too. Knowing what you hate is just as useful as knowing what you love.

### What if I'm not in the Indianapolis area?
Reid Design is currently focused on in-person work in the Indianapolis area, so projects further out aren't a fit right now. If you're in a neighboring region and the drive works, reach out and we'll see what's possible.

### Do you offer payment plans?
For larger full-service projects, fees are structured in milestones, a deposit at signing, a second payment at concept presentation, and a final payment at installation. For smaller packages like consultations and Shopping & Sourcing hours, full payment is required upfront.

### What areas does Reid Design serve?
Plainfield, Indianapolis, and the surrounding communities, Carmel, Fishers, Westfield, Zionsville, Noblesville, Geist, McCordsville, Broad Ripple, and nearby neighborhoods. Homes within about 30 minutes of Plainfield are covered with no travel fee. Further-out homes are welcome too, just with a small travel fee that's quoted upfront.

### Are there extra fees for suburban clients?
Most suburbs are within the no-travel-fee zone, including Carmel, Fishers, Westfield, Zionsville, Noblesville, and Plainfield. The pricing on the services page is the same regardless of which of those suburbs you're in. For homes 45 minutes or more from Plainfield, a small travel fee covers the drive time, $50 for 45 to 75 minutes, $75 to $100 for 75 to 120 minutes. Always quoted upfront before booking.

### How long does a project take?
The consultation is a single 60 to 90 minute visit. The design plan typically takes 2 to 3 weeks to build after the consultation. From there, shopping and styling timing depends on scope and on furniture lead times, anywhere from a few weeks for in-stock items to several months for custom pieces. Hourly Shopping & Sourcing turnaround depends on what you need. I'll always give you a realistic estimate, not a best-case scenario.

### How does trade vendor access work?
I have accounts with vendors not open to the public. These lines offer more distinctive pieces, and my trade pricing is passed along to you, frequently offsetting a portion of the design fee.

### What should I prepare before the consultation?
Not much, but a few things help. Take a few photos of the room or rooms you want to address, including the corners and any areas that frustrate you. If you've been collecting inspiration on Pinterest or Instagram, save the link or have it ready to share. Think about your budget range, even a loose one, so we can talk realistically about scope. Most important: be honest about what you don't like. That's more useful than describing what you want.
